correctness.rationale: Both variants have the same integral cycle group in degree one. Group allowed two-paths by ordered endpoints: a forbidden shortcut requires zero total coefficient on its endpoint fiber, a permitted shortcut has no constraint, and diagonal fibers are unconstrained only in the regular complex. Thus the quotient of boundary groups is generated by the actual backtracks B_uv. Diagonal-fiber differences identify all incident-edge backtracks, and the sum of two directed triangle boundaries kills the corresponding component generator. In a triangle-free component the signed boundary of every admissible generator has total arc coefficient zero, whereas B_uv has total arc coefficient 2, giving infinite order and independent generators in different components. Isolated vertices make no contribution. Inclusions send a representing cycle to precisely the same cycle in the larger graph, so the stated merge and death maps follow; no splitting is used.
residual_risks: Recorded 1103 comparisons are mod two and were not rerun; they do not establish the integral result, any universal characteristic-two rule, or the inclusion maps. The integral generator and detection argument is decisive.

evidence: Chaplin's integral motif generators are for all finite digraphs, not just symmetric ones. Muranov–Muranova's categorical transfers do not compare these two degree-one groups; the acyclic persistence record has no backtracks.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader integral presentation applies directly after specializing every edge to reciprocal arcs. The other broader-sounding works address different invariants.

evidence: The only added relations come from backtrack boundaries. At each base vertex the diagonal coefficient vanishes precisely for combinations of backtracks with zero coefficient sum. In a symmetric graph these give B_uv−B_uw along incidents; a directed triangle and its initial-edge reversal sum to B_uv; all remaining triangle-free nonregular boundaries have zero total arc coefficient.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The quotient already has one common backtrack per edge component; the displayed triangle relation kills it when present and coefficient sum detects its exact infinite order otherwise. The same cycles commute with inclusion, giving merge or death without an additional topological theorem. The full claimed invariant follows by a short, direct calculation in the existing presentation.

evidence: Chaplin's Propositions 3.14, 3.15 and 3.17 identify the common low-degree chains, integral inclusion and complete integral regular two-path generators. Corollary 3.19 writes the nonregular chains in those generators; nonregularity imposes zero sum at each diagonal shortcut.
The cyclic-Hasse facet-adjacency result concerns a different digraph and homology group, not a reformulation of this comparison.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Taking the quotient of the published boundary presentations gives exactly the regularization kernel; changing vocabulary from directed double edge to backtrack does not alter it.

evidence: The top indexed component-gap record is the assigned record itself; inspected distinct same-date records are about cyclic Hasse graphs or acyclic persistence. Published motifs and cycle examples give individual regular/nonregular comparisons.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Those examples are not an exhaustive table for arbitrary symmetric orientations and do not by themselves imply the claim. The decisive coverage is the general presentation, not a lookup of particular rank differences.

originality.rationale: No inspected source was found to state the global sequence in that wording, but it is mechanically implied by the existing integral boundary presentation and the canonical representing cycles. This is verified prior coverage by implication, not a finding of verbatim duplication or a guess based on a search hit.
residual_risks: No claim of exhaustive historical priority or of a verbatim earlier theorem. The rejection rests on the direct mathematical implication of an accessible earlier primary result, not on catalog ordering or uninspected literature.
